title: 10 Polynomial arithmetic: Visual Guide
outline: 1. Stack By Degree | two cubics on six coefficient sliders, added or subtracted in a column ledger with the wrong add-the-exponents answer shown beside the right one | adding and subtracting combine coefficients within one degree and never move an exponent, and a column that totals zero is how the degree can drop

2. Why Cubes Cancel | the difference and sum of cubes with the cubed number on a slider, the six-term expansion shown cancelling in pairs, and four candidate factorizations to test by multiplying back | the cube patterns work because the four middle products annihilate in two pairs, which forces the binomial's sign, the trinomial's opposite middle sign and the constant b squared

3. Factor Until It Stops | seven expressions factored one press at a time, with each factor tagged linear, irreducible or still factorable, and the roots read off by the zero-product property | factor completely means keep applying patterns until every factor is linear or an irreducible quadratic like a sum of squares, then check the degrees sum to the original

4. Slide The Secant | four polynomials with draggable endpoints a and b, the secant line drawn against the dashed tangent, and the correct quotient beside the three classic wrong expressions | average rate of change is (f(b) - f(a)) / (b - a), the slope of the secant through the endpoints, and it is neither the total change, nor the tangent slope, nor a midpoint value
